When the cursor is placed before an indented token on a new line, pressing `Cmd + Shift + ←` should jump to the end of the previous line, allowing a single Backspace to delete all indentation and pull the token up. 

```ts
const memberships = await this.entityManager.find(
    CompanyMembershipEntity,
    ...
```

Starting point:

```ts
find(
    |CompanyMembershipEntity,
```

**Actual behavior:**

Problem 1 – `Press Cmd + Shift + ←` once:

```ts
find(
|    CompanyMembershipEntity,
```
Cursor moves to the beginning of the line, before all spaces.
Now I have to press Backspace 2 times (or however many spaces / tabs there are) to delete the indentation.

Problem 2 – Press `Cmd + Shift + ←` twice:

```ts
const memberships = await this.entityManager|.find(
    CompanyMembershipEntity,
```

Cursor jumps further left to the previous line, often before .find, skipping completely over the opening parenthesis.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/15887ea1-6b0a-4012-84bb-b9b603d79d4c

Expected behavior:

Press `Cmd + Shift + ←` once:

```ts
find(|
    CompanyMembershipEntity,
```
Cursor moves directly after the opening parenthesis ( on the previous line.

Then press `Backspace` once:

```ts
find(|CompanyMembershipEntity,
    where,
    { populate }
);
```

All indentation is deleted with ONE keystroke – the entire block of spaces is removed at once, and CompanyMembershipEntity is now on the same line as `find(`.

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: No, it's a bug with the extension API itself

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.135.0-insider (Universal)
- OS Version: Darwin arm64 25.4.0

Hello, I'm reporting a bug I've noticed where calling `cancelSelection` interferes with extensions that register the `"type"` command. Normally extensions can register `"type"` to intercept all inputs:

```
subscription = vscode.commands.registerCommand("type", onType)
```

This is useful for Vim-style extensions which want to override regular typed letters like "a", "b", "c". Typing those letters are instead intercepted by the `onType` listener, and don't actually type letters.

However, I noticed that when I trigger a `"cancelSelection"` command, the next typed letter will actually get typed, somehow bypassing the `"type"` register command:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b48758c2-b450-4fd1-9acd-7e2bcd05337e

In the above recording I have a `"type"` command registered, configured so that typing the letter "a" will trigger the `"cancelSelection"` command, and typing the letter "j" will trigger the `"cursorDown"` command.

When I press "j" I would expect the cursor to move down one row.

Instead, when I press "j" it removes most of the section I had previously highlighted, only keeping a couple letters. Then it adds "jj".

Some extra information:
* This issue began occurring sometime between 2026-01-01 and 2026-04-23 on stable
* My extension I used to reproduce this (`bmalehorn.vimspired`) hasn't been updated in 3 years, so it's not a change in the extension. You can view the extension source [here](https://github.com/bmalehorn/vscode-vimspired/blob/578eeb3b80979ac87d33799b8485475503f910b4/src/extension.ts)
* It's possible this is a regression in the extension API, and I'd be fine with a workaround my extension can use
* Canceling selection by pressing Escape does not reproduce the issue (so, what's the difference between Escape and `cancelSelection`?)
* This doesn't occur on reverse selection (selecting from right to left)
* This doesn't occur on multiline selections
* The amount of text remaining (above, only 1 character remained) is not consistently 1 character, it's a variable amount between 0 and the whole line
* Different keys (a, j) and different commands (cursorDown) still reproduce the issue


Steps to Reproduce:

1. Install the extension `bmalehorn.vimspired`
2. Set your vscode config to:
```json
{
  "vimspired.keybindings": {
    "a": "cancelSelection",
    "j": "cursorDown",
  },
}
```
3. in a file, highlight one line from left to right
4. press "a"
5. press "j"

Expected: the cursor moves down 1 row, no text is modified.
Actual: the previously-highlighted portion is partially deleted and "jj" is added to the end.

title: Render evidence chapters from the automation harness
body:
Follow-up to #331558 (merged), which added `VSCODE_EVIDENCE_CLEAN_CAPTURE=1`. Rebased onto `main`, so this diff now contains only the changes below.

## Summary

Moves evidence chaptering into the harness so a **clean capture can still be annotated**.

#331558 stopped the step banner being drawn into the window under test, but left nothing in its place: a local run produced an unannotated recording. This adds the annotation back as a post-processing step.

## Changes

- **`videoStartedAt` is recorded natively.** Both launchers stamp the moment the recording context is created and pass it to `PlaywrightDriver`; the evidence manifest exports it. Without an origin, captured step timestamps cannot be converted into offsets in the video.
- **`test/mcp/scripts/render-evidence-chapters.mjs`** composes a full-screen card before each step, using the manifest's step timestamps and statuses. Cards are *inserted between segments* rather than overlaid, so no recorded frame is hidden.
- The skill documents `--build` for targeting an installed Insiders, and the chaptering command.

Rendering is non-fatal: without `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` it warns and leaves the raw recording untouched.

## Why here rather than in the caller

`microsoft/vscode-engineering` already runs this harness in CI and currently carries its own copy of the renderer, plus two source patches that re-implement what is now supported directly:

| CI patch | Replaced by |
|---|---|
| rewrites `showOverlay` to a no-op | `VSCODE_EVIDENCE_CLEAN_CAPTURE=1` (#331558) |
| injects a video start anchor into `playwrightBrowser.ts` | `videoStartedAt` in the manifest |
| its own `render-video-chapters.mjs` | `test/mcp/scripts/render-evidence-chapters.mjs` |

Those patches only exist because the harness could not do this itself. A follow-up in that repo will delete them and call this script; both local runs and CI then share one implementation.

The Electron path gains an anchor too, which the CI patch never covered — it only patched the browser launcher.

## Validation

- `npm --prefix test/mcp run compile` passes
- rendered a synthetic run end to end with real ffmpeg: output was exactly `60s raw + 3s intro + 2 × 2.5s cards = 68.000s`, and a frame sampled after the first card showed raw footage at the expected offset, confirming alignment
- verified the no-ffmpeg path warns and leaves the recording unchanged

> Authored with Copilot

title: agentHost: Collect and package debug logs on the host
body:
## Summary

Reworks **Developer: Export Agent Host Debug Logs** so the Agent Host owns discovery and packaging of host-side diagnostics instead of the client guessing host filesystem paths.

- Adds a typed private AHP extension request, `vscode/collectAgentHostDebugLogs`, returning an opaque artifact URI.
- Uses the Copilot SDK's `session.rpc.debug.collectLogs` API for SDK-owned events, process logs, and shell logs.
- Keeps client-owned logs on the client: window/shared-process output, AHP JSONL transport logs, remote-forwarded channels, and usage/customization sidecars.
- Produces one final ZIP; native exports flatten the Agent Host archive into it.
- Supports export with or without an active session. With a session, SDK events/shell logs are included. Without one, collection remains host-wide and excludes unrelated session events/shell logs.

## Remote transfer

The artifact contract is a URI, not inline bytes.

- Local Agent Host artifacts are ordinary local `file:` URIs and never transfer archive bytes over IPC.
- Remote Agent Host artifacts are downloaded through the private `vscode/readAgentHostDebugLogsChunk` request in bounded 1 MiB chunks.
- The old whole-file Base64 read path is not used as a fallback.
- The chunk reader only serves artifacts produced and retained by the collector; it is not a general-purpose remote file read.

## Safety and lifecycle

- Bounds archive bytes, staged bytes, individual files, and archive entry count.
- Keeps the tail of oversized logs so recent failures remain diagnosable.
- Validates ZIP entry count/expanded size before flattening and rejects duplicate final paths.
- Expires abandoned host artifacts and cleans staging/artifacts on completion and shutdown.
- Validates the returned artifact URI scheme, kind, and declared sizes.
- Verifies actual streamed byte count against the declared artifact size.
- SDK/provider collection failures surface to the user instead of silently switching to a second path-guessing implementation.

## Compatibility

This intentionally uses the existing private AHP extension-method seam rather than changing the generated public protocol while the shape settles. A remote host that predates the request returns `MethodNotFound` as an explicit collection failure.

## Validation

- Client typecheck and full product/Copilot compile pass.
- Agent Host, chat browser, Agents provider, ZIP, protocol routing, and streaming tests pass.
- Layer validation and hygiene pass.
- Manually verified in Code OSS:
  - Active Copilot session ZIP includes `agenthost.log`, SDK `events.jsonl`/process logs, and client-owned logs.
  - No-active/New Session ZIP includes host/window/shared/AHP/process logs without unrelated `events.jsonl`.
  - Active Codex session produces the common host artifact without Copilot-specific entries.
  - Repeated exports leave no temporary artifacts.

(Written by Copilot)

title: chat sessions are gone
body:
After a normal VS Code restart, two days’ worth of chat sessions are completely gone. I checked every filter—they weren’t hidden; they were deleted.

This isn’t an isolated issue either. I’ve had this happen several times, along with Copilot dropping file changes even after I click Keep, inconsistent edits when sessions error or retry, repeated parts inside an answer, and other reliability problems.

It’s genuinely frustrating. VS Code Chat still feels like an early beta product, and I’m seriously considering moving to something more reliable.

Version: 1.133.0

**opus findings:**

> Chat history is silently lost when a window transitions between single-folder and multi-root workspace storage. On VS Code 1.133.0 (a5b5009513, macOS arm64), adding a second folder to a single-folder window promotes it to an untitled workspace with a new workspaceStorage hash, and ChatSessionStore logs Workspace transition from <oldHash> to <newHash> / Copied N chat session files … (originals preserved at old location). The transition copies the chatSessions/*.jsonl transcripts to the new storage folder but does not migrate the chat.ChatSessionStore.index key in state.vscdb. All subsequent sessions are indexed only under the new hash, so the moment you return to the plain folder the chat list is frozen at the timestamp of the transition — in my case it jumped straight from Aug 17 14:02 to Aug 19, hiding 22 sessions (13 of them from a full day's work) even though all 144 .jsonl files were sitting in the folder untouched. The loss is invisible: no error, no warning, and the history simply appears truncated. It is also effectively unrecoverable through the UI, because the untitled workspace's Code/Workspaces/<id>/workspace.json had already been cleaned up, leaving its 84-entry index reachable only by opening state.vscdb in sqlite3 by hand. Suggested fix: migrate the index entries alongside the transcript files during a workspace transition (or reconcile the index against the chatSessions/ directory on startup, which would repair the orphaned files automatically).

title: Reject null in vObjAny()
body:
### Problem

`TypeofValidator` compares `typeof content` against the expected type name:

```ts
if (typeof content !== this.type) {
    return { content: undefined, error: { message: `Expected ${this.type}, but got ${typeof content}` } };
}
```

`typeof null === 'object'`, and `vObjAny()` is `new TypeofValidator('object')`. So null passes validation:

```
vObjAny().validate(null)   ->  { content: null, error: undefined }
```

Two things that makes wrong:

- The declared type is `ValidatorBase<object>`, and TypeScript's `object` excludes `null`. A caller trusting the result gets a `null` the types say cannot be there.
- Its own `getJSONSchema()` returns `{ type: 'object' }`, and in JSON Schema `object` excludes null too (`null` is a separate type). The validator contradicts the schema it advertises.

`ObjValidator`, in the same file, already guards exactly this:

```ts
if (typeof content !== 'object' || content === null) {
    return { content: undefined, error: { message: 'Expected object' } };
}
```

And the one in-tree caller works around it, re-checking after a *successful* validation — `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/claude/claudeSubagentResolver.ts`:

```ts
const r = vObjAny().validate(input);
if (r.error || r.content === null || Array.isArray(r.content)) {
    return undefined;
}
```

That `r.content === null` branch only exists because `vObjAny()` lets null through.

### Change

Reject null for the `'object'` case, and report it as `null` rather than `object` so the message is accurate for every typeof validator. `vString().validate(null)` previously said *"Expected string, but got object"*.

Before / after, running the real module:

| input | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `vObjAny().validate(null)` | `OK content=null` | `Expected object, but got null` |
| `vObjAny().validate({a:1})` | `OK` | `OK` (unchanged) |
| `vObjAny().validate([1,2])` | `OK` | `OK` (unchanged) |
| `vObjAny().validate('str')` | `Expected object, but got string` | unchanged |
| `vString().validate(null)` | `Expected string, but got object` | `Expected string, but got null` |

Arrays still pass, as before — only null changes.

I left the `r.content === null` check in `claudeSubagentResolver.ts` alone. It is now redundant but still correct, and it guards untrusted SDK JSON; removing it felt like the wrong thing to bundle into this fix.

### Tests

Added `src/vs/base/test/common/validation.test.ts` — the module had no tests. It covers null rejection, that objects and arrays still pass, non-object rejection, and the corrected `null` message on the other typeof validators.

### Verification

I could not run the repo's test harness — I worked from a sparse checkout (`src/vs/base`, `src/vs/platform`, `src/vs/editor/common`) because a full clone kept timing out here, so there is no `node_modules` to build against. What I did run:

- Executed the real `validation.ts` module directly to produce the before/after table above, with the fix stashed and unstashed.
- `tsc --strict --noEmit` on `validation.ts`: **no errors**.
- The 8 errors `tsc` reports for `validation.test.ts` are all `Cannot find name 'suite'/'test'` and `Cannot find module 'assert'`. I checked this is environmental: running the identical command against the existing `src/vs/base/test/common/numbers.test.ts` produces 9 errors of the same class.

So the test file has not been executed by the real runner. Worth a CI run before merging, and I am happy to adjust if it disagrees with local conventions.

### Note

`TypeOfMap` also has a `null: null` entry, but no validator is ever constructed with it, and it could not work as written for the same `typeof` reason. Left alone as out of scope — flagging it in case it is meant to be used.

title: Render an embedded attachment that has no content type
body:
Fixes #331568.

A pasted image renders as a broken thumbnail because its attachment was persisted without a `contentType`, and the restore path reads that field unguarded:

```ts
if (!attachment.contentType.startsWith('image/')) {
```

Evaluated in the running workbench against the exact record from a real session database:

```
{"type":"embeddedResource","label":"Pasted Image","displayKind":"image","data":"iVBORw0KGgo…"}

(s) => s.contentType.startsWith("image/")
→ TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'startsWith')
```

### Fix

The guard lives in `state/sessionState.ts`, the hand-written layer where VS Code-specific helpers over the generated protocol types already live:

```ts
export function embeddedAttachmentContentType(attachment: { contentType?: string; displayKind?: string }): string | undefined {
	return attachment.contentType ?? (attachment.displayKind === 'image' ? 'image/png' : undefined);
}
```

`displayKind` already records that the attachment is an image, so the type is inferred from what the record states rather than assumed. An attachment with neither falls through to the generic branch instead of being treated as an image.

Three call sites now resolve the content type through it: `stateToProgressAdapter.ts`, `codexPromptResolver.ts`, and `copilotAgentSession.ts`.

### Why this does not change the protocol type

An earlier revision of this PR made `contentType` optional in `state/protocol/channels-chat/state.ts`. That was wrong twice over, and both commits are kept so the reasoning is visible.

That file is generated output. It carries `DO NOT EDIT -- auto-generated by scripts/sync-agent-host-protocol.ts` and is synced from `microsoft/agent-host-protocol`, so the next sync would have silently reverted the change.

It was also the wrong request to make of the protocol. Upstream declares `contentType` as required, and every current producer in this repo sets it (`agentHostSessionHandler.ts` in all four places, and `copilot/mapSessionEvents.ts`). A record without one is therefore not a protocol gap; it is a record written by an older build that is still on disk. The helper's parameter is structural rather than `MessageEmbeddedResourceAttachment` precisely because the record it defends against is one the declared type says cannot exist, and the tests construct it the same way and say so.

### Verification

- Three tests over the real persisted shape: an image with no content type restores as an image, a declared content type still wins, and a non-image with no content type restores as generic. The first and third fail if the guard is removed; the second passes either way by design, since it guards against the inference overriding a declared type.
- Confirmed in the running workbench: the shipped expression throws on that record, the fixed one returns `true` and hands on `image/png`, and a non-image with no content type returns `false`.
- `tsc --noEmit` reports no errors in any of the touched files.

### Notes

Every current producer defaults the field, so newly pasted images were never affected. This repairs attachments already written, which otherwise stay broken for the life of the session, and which no producer-side change can reach.

I have not identified which producer wrote a record without the field. The one I have predates the build I could inspect, and I would rather say so than name a suspect I cannot demonstrate.

title: A pasted image renders as a broken thumbnail when its attachment has no contentType
body:
A pasted image in an agent session renders as a broken thumbnail. The bytes are fine and the model receives the image; only the workbench fails to display it.

### Cause

The attachment is persisted without a `contentType`. Taken from a real session database:

```json
{"type":"embeddedResource","label":"Pasted Image","displayKind":"image","data":"iVBORw0KGgo…"}
```

There is no `contentType` key anywhere in that database. The restore path reads it unguarded:

```ts
if (attachment.type === MessageAttachmentKind.EmbeddedResource) {
	if (!attachment.contentType.startsWith('image/')) {
```

so restoring the attachment throws and it never renders. Evaluated in the running workbench against that exact record:

```
(s) => s.contentType.startsWith("image/")
→ TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'startsWith')
```

`MessageEmbeddedResourceAttachment.contentType` is declared as a required `string`, so nothing in the type system anticipated the value the wire actually carries.

### Scope

`contentType` is dereferenced without a guard in four places: `stateToProgressAdapter` (the one users see), `codexPromptResolver` (twice) and `copilotAgentSession`.

Every current producer defaults the field, so newly pasted images are unaffected. This is about attachments already on disk, which stay broken for the life of the session.

### Reproduction

Any session whose stored attachment lacks `contentType` renders that attachment as a broken image. I have not identified which producer wrote one without it, and I would rather report that honestly than guess: the record predates the build I could inspect.

### Description

When a Copilot agent uses a file-search or file-reading tool against the current workspace while in WSL, VS Code prompts:

> Allow reading file outside of workspace?

The requested directory is the active workspace itself, not a path outside it.

This occurred both when the tool explicitly supplied the workspace's absolute path and when the tool omitted the path and relied on its current-working-directory default.

I used `--disable-extensions .` to disable all extensions (except WSL, which is enabled automatically) and it occurs the same way.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a WSL folder as the workspace in VS Code Insiders. For example, open a terminal at a dir like this:

   `/home/dagood/try/copilot-confused-workspace`

   And run `code-insiders .`.

2. Start a Copilot agent chat by asking it to do some ordinary modification.
3. See the agent invoke a glob/file-search operation with:

   ```json
   {
     "pattern": "**/*",
     "paths": "/home/dagood/try/copilot-confused-workspace"
   }
   ```

4. Observe the "Allow reading file outside of workspace?" prompt.

If you then get Copilot to invoke the same tool without an explicit path, the same outside-of-workspace prompt appears again.

```json
{
  "pattern": "**/*"
}
```

### Expected behavior

File operations whose resolved target is inside the active workspace should not trigger the outside-of-workspace permission prompt.

Omitting the path should use the agent's workspace working directory and should likewise not be classified as external access.

### Actual behavior

VS Code presents the outside-of-workspace permission prompt for both:

- An explicit absolute path exactly equal to the active workspace root.
- A glob operation with no path argument, which defaults to the agent's current working directory.

The second dialog displays the workspace name (`copilot-confused-workspace`) as the target even though the tool input contains only:

```json
{
  "pattern": "**/*"
}
```

### Verification that the path is inside the workspace

The agent process reported:

```text
$ pwd
/home/dagood/try/copilot-confused-workspace

$ readlink -f .
/home/dagood/try/copilot-confused-workspace

$ readlink -f /home/dagood/try/copilot-confused-workspace
/home/dagood/try/copilot-confused-workspace
```

The current directory and requested directory resolve to exactly the same path. There is no symlink mismatch or other filesystem anomaly.

title: chat: add a render-only Permissions area to the Customizations editor
body:
Adds a **Permissions** group to the Chat Customizations editor sidebar — Terminal, Files and Network — behind the off-by-default `chat.customizations.permissions.enabled` setting.

Today the only way to see what governs an agent is `Developer: Policy Diagnostics`, which dumps raw JSON for the managed slice. This gives users a real answer to *"why did it ask me?"* and *"what did my org lock down?"*.

> [!NOTE]
> Draft. The UI can only populate one of five permission layers until the runtime exposes a read API for its resolved rule set — tracked in `github/copilot-sdk-internal#244`. See *Known limitation* below.

## The design constraint

**The Copilot runtime is the source of truth for permissions.** It owns the rule DSL, the matcher, and the precedence between managed policy, configured rules, location grants and session grants. This PR is deliberately **render-only** and re-derives none of it:

- `chatPermissionRuleSyntax.ts` only splits `Kind(argument)` for display, and says so in its own header.
- Domains exist **only** for the four rule families `parse_managed_rule` accepts — `Shell`/`Bash`/`PowerShell`, `Read`, `Edit`/`Write`, `Domain`. MCP servers and built-in tools are governed by different contracts and get no domain until the runtime can report rules for them.
- Managed rules render read-only.

This follows the `policy-and-managed-settings` skill: *"Do not duplicate a runtime parser, matcher, or security decision in VS Code."*

## Known limitation (why it's a draft)

The runtime exposes no read API for its resolved rule set — only the managed slice, via the slow `getManagedSettings()` diagnostics probe. So the snapshot reports **only** `ChatPermissionScope.Managed` and the UI explicitly names the layers it could not read.

That honesty is deliberate and load-bearing. `ChatPermissionSnapshot` distinguishes `loading` / `unavailable` / `error` / `available`, every `available` snapshot carries `resolvedScopes`, and a provider that fails is surfaced rather than dropped. **Rendering an empty list would assert "nothing governs this agent" — the opposite of the truth under `failClosed`.**

When the runtime ships the projection, `browser/permissions/chatPermissionSnapshotService.ts` is the only file that changes.

## Design language

The sections deliberately reuse the customization sections' chrome rather than approximating it — they join the same selector lists for the content panel, the title header (title / description / inline learn-more), the search row and the collapsible group headers, so consistency holds by construction.

What stays different is what a row *means*: a permission rule is a read-only statement of what the runtime enforces, not something authored here. So there is no create button (the primary-action slot holds **Refresh**), uneditable rows carry a lock, each row ends in an allow/ask/deny pill, and a rule overridden by a higher layer is struck through with a `→ 🔒 Managed Ask` badge naming the winner.

## Screenshots

Covered by four component fixtures (`chatPermissionsSection.fixture.ts`), each in Dark and Light: managed-only, all scopes with a shadowed rule, partial provider failure, and unavailable.

## Reviewer notes

Bugs found and fixed during review passes, worth a look since they're the risky parts of the diff:

**Sidebar refactor** (the `WorkbenchList` went from `ISectionItem` to a union including non-selectable group headers, so indices now refer to `sidebarItems`, not `sections`):
1. `layoutSidebar` still sized from `sections.length * 26`, ignoring the 28px headers, clipping the last rows.
2. Blank pane on harness switch — this change *introduced* the path, since the previous contributed section was Codex-only while permissions use `supportsHarness: () => true`.

**Snapshot correctness:**
3. Disabling the agent host mid-probe left the in-flight generation valid, so a late result could overwrite the disabled state.
4. Provider failures arrive in-band as `{ error }`, not thrown. Skipping them made a timeout look like "not supported", and a mixed result could present one provider's rules as the whole policy. Now: all-failed → `error`; partial → `available` + a warning banner listing who failed.
5. Selecting a permission section focused the hidden prompts search box; contributed sections now route through their own `focus()` via one shared helper.

Also note `allow-auto-only` is read from the raw managed slice: it's in the runtime's `managed-settings-schema.json` and enforced in `managed.rs`, but the bundled SDK typings still declare only `"disable"`. The resolved `bypassPermissionsDisabled` / `failClosed` verdict is treated as a floor the raw settings may refine but never soften.

## Validation

- `tsc -p src/tsconfig.json` clean; `valid-layers-check` passes
- `npm run eslint` clean
- 48 tests pass (`chatPermission` + `aiCustomization`)
- 8 component fixtures render without errors
- Hygiene/pre-commit hook passes (it caught invalid CSS font-size tokens and indentation along the way)

title: Show delegated child chats/sessions in the Agent Sessions UI

labels.name: feature-request
labels.description: Request for new features or functionality

body:
## Feature request

Surface cross-session delegation without making child sessions the primary unit of work.

Related orchestration work: #331521 and #331518.

## Product model

A session is the user-visible unit of work: one workspace/worktree, lifecycle, and aggregate diff. Parallel subtasks that share that unit should use chats within the session.

Child sessions are reserved for work that needs an independent workspace, worktree or branch, provider, or lifecycle. Their UI should remain secondary while still making ownership and integration status understandable.

## Current behavior

Sessions created through `create_session` appear as ordinary entries in the Agent Sessions list. The UI does not show that another session delegated them, where their changes live, or whether their result has been integrated.

## Proposed experience

- Keep the creator session and its aggregate result primary.
- Show a compact, optionally expanded summary of independently scoped child sessions.
- Display each child's label, title, provider, workspace/worktree, status, and linked PR when available.
- Provide an action to open or reveal a child.
- Make it clear whether changes are in the parent worktree or remain in an independent child branch/worktree.
- Avoid always nesting every implementation-detail child in the main sessions list.
- Preserve relationships across reloads and session restoration.
- Continue showing relationships to the user when model-to-creator coordination is disabled; `coordinateWithCreator` is a model communication boundary, not a user-visibility boundary.

The UI should consume the provider-neutral orchestration metadata introduced by #331518 rather than infer relationships from titles, workspaces, or provider-specific state.

## Acceptance criteria

- A user can identify independently scoped work delegated by the current session.
- The parent remains the clear owner of the overall task and aggregate result.
- A user can tell where each child's changes live and open the correct session or PR.
- Relationships and statuses survive reloads without overwhelming the active-session list.
- The presentation works consistently across agent providers.

title: Support deferred workspace binding for folderless agent sessions

labels.name: feature-request
labels.description: Request for new features or functionality

labels.name: verification-needed
labels.description: Verification of issue is requested

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

body:
## Feature request

Allow an agent chat/session to start without a folder or workspace, then bind it to the appropriate workspace later after the request and conversation context provide enough information.

Related workspace discovery work: #330948 and #331525.

## Motivation

The correct workspace is not always known when a chat starts. A user may begin with a general request, refer to a project naturally later, or ask the agent to investigate before deciding where work belongs. Requiring an up-front folder either interrupts the flow or risks selecting an unrelated current/recent workspace.

Workspace discovery provides candidate workspaces, but there is currently no end-to-end flow for starting folderless and applying the selected workspace to the existing conversation.

## Proposed behavior

- Permit creating an agent chat/session without an initial folder or workspace.
- Keep the session folderless while handling requests that do not require workspace access.
- Resolve a workspace later from the user's request, attached context, or an explicit workspace-discovery result.
- Ask the user when resolution is ambiguous or would expand filesystem access.
- Bind the selected workspace to the existing session without losing its conversation.
- Initialize workspace-dependent configuration, customizations, source control, tools, and provider state after binding.
- Support local and remote workspace URIs.
- Avoid silently selecting an arbitrary recent workspace when there is no confident match.

The first successful binding should establish the session's workspace. Changing an already-bound session to an unrelated workspace can remain a separate capability.

## Example

1. A user opens a new folderless chat and asks, “Investigate the flaky authentication tests.”
2. The agent uses the request and known-workspace context to identify likely repositories.
3. If one match is clear, the agent proposes or selects it according to existing permission policy; if several match, it asks the user.
4. The existing chat becomes bound to that workspace and continues the task with its conversation intact.

## Acceptance criteria

- A new agent session can remain folderless until workspace access is needed.
- A workspace can be selected and attached after session creation.
- Existing conversation history survives the transition.
- Ambiguous or permission-expanding choices require user confirmation.
- Workspace-dependent state is initialized consistently after binding.
- No unrelated workspace is selected as an implicit fallback.

title: agentHost: report completed model calls per turn
body:
https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/8738

## Overview

### What

Adds `modelCallCount` to the existing per-turn `agentHost.turnCompleted` telemetry event. The measurement reports completed upstream model-response rounds attributed directly to the turn, including responses that request tools and the final tool-free response.

Before this change, equivalent turn-depth analysis was available only for a subset of Copilot turns through `toolCallDetails.numRequests`. After this change, the turn event carries the rollup across Copilot, Claude, and Codex, including turns without tool details.

Provider-native completion boundaries remain intact:

- Copilot uses the response's `apiCallId`, with stable request/message fallbacks, and collapses split assistant messages from one API call.
- Claude uses completed canonical assistant messages and excludes aborted streams.
- Codex uses cumulative per-response token-usage snapshots, retaining a session baseline so replayed and rate-limit-only updates do not increment the count.

The host routes model-call signals through the existing active-turn and subagent mapping, then deduplicates provider call identities in `AgentHostTurnTracker` before emitting the final count.

### Why

Turn-level model-call depth helps identify expensive or looping turns and correlate them with latency, failures, interaction modes, model selection, and subagent use. Keeping the rollup on `agentHost.turnCompleted` avoids a Copilot-only tool-event join and gives the same analysis across Agent Host providers.

## Property-by-property parity

No properties are added or changed.

## Measurement-by-measurement parity

| Measurement | Source | Parity |
|---|---|---|
| `modelCallCount` | Deduplicated completed response boundaries from Copilot `assistant.message`, Claude canonical assistant messages, and Codex per-response usage updates | ✅ Same completed model-response-round signal across providers |

Failed provider attempts that never complete a response are deliberately excluded. Existing per-call response telemetry remains the source for attempt-level reliability analysis.

## Row-count and dashboard implications

- Event cadence remains one `agentHost.turnCompleted` row per tracked turn.
- New rows carry a numeric count, including `0` when no completed response was observed.
- Historical rows have no `modelCallCount`; queries must not treat missing historical values as zero.
- Main-agent and subagent calls are attributed to their own turn rows.
- Copilot rollout can be checked by joining to `toolCallDetails` on turn ID and comparing against `numRequests`.

## Semantic-shift ledger

| Field | Shift | Impact |
|---|---|---|
| `modelCallCount` versus provider attempts | Counts completed model responses, not failed retries or transport attempts | Supports turn-depth and loop analysis; attempt-level failure rates continue to use response telemetry |

title: Remote tunnel service status client can take over tunnel ownership
body:
Type: Bug

When Remote Tunnel Access is enabled as a service, the desktop shared process starts a second `code-tunnel tunnel` process so the UI can stream the installed service singleton's logs and machine status. That process is intended to be a client only.

Current behavior

The coordinator launches the status client with normal hosting arguments, including `--name`, `--user-data-dir`, and `--delegate-to-editor`. When it connects to the service singleton, the CLI warns:

```text
Command-line options will not be applied until the existing tunnel exits.
```

More importantly, `serve_with_csa()` loops back through `acquire_singleton()` after a disconnect. During a service restart, the UI status client can acquire the singleton lock and become the tunnel owner. In a live trace this temporarily changed the hosted tunnel tags from the persisted service name to the desktop-derived hostname; after launchd recovered ownership, the tags changed back. The UI process is also parent-bound, so this defeats the service lifetime contract.

Expected behavior

The desktop child used for service status must only attach/retry as a client and must never acquire tunnel ownership. It should not pass hosting arguments that an existing singleton cannot apply. The UI should report the name emitted by the running service, not the ignored requested name. If service installation fails, the existing named in-session hosting fallback should remain intact.

Competing explanations checked

- No `remote.tunnels.access.hostNameOverride` or related remote-tunnel setting is configured in the affected profile/workspace.
- The differing requested name is the normal hostname-derived default; the installed service has its own persisted tunnel identity.
- This is built-in Remote Tunnel Access behavior, not a conflict between installed Remote Tunnel extensions.
- The service itself remained healthy and connected; deleting the desktop child would regress UI readiness/status reporting.

Source boundary

- `src/vs/platform/remoteTunnel/node/tunnelProcessCoordinator.ts` constructs the service status child as a normal hosting command.
- `cli/src/commands/tunnels.rs` uses the same acquire-or-host loop for both actual hosts and attached status clients.

Reproduced in VS Code 1.133.0. The same argument/ownership path is present on current `main` (1.135.0).

title: Notify creators when delegated sessions need attention
body:
Depends on #331518.
Fixes #331521.

## Summary

Add opt-in lifecycle notifications from delegated child sessions to their creator after the foundational orchestration relationships in #331518.

- Extend `create_session` with `notifyOnIdle: "once" | "always"`.
- Arm notification delivery when a child starts work.
- Notify its creator when the child needs input, becomes idle, or errors.
- Suppress duplicate terminal notifications and rearm `always` notifications on the next work cycle.
- Observe exact session-status transitions so queued work cannot hide a completed cycle.
- Restore a cold creator before delivery.
- Queue a system notification instead of replacing an active creator turn.
- Persist notification state and consume it only after dispatch so failed creator resolution can retry.

## User benefits

- Notice blocked delegated work without repeatedly checking each child session.
- Run parallel investigations or implementation tasks and receive updates in the creator conversation.
- Preserve notification policy and delivery state when sessions are evicted and restored.
- Avoid child completions interrupting or replacing active creator work.

## Why this is separate

Notification delivery introduces lifecycle observation, deduplication, restoration, and concurrency behavior beyond the durable lineage and discovery model in #331518. Keeping it stacked makes those concerns independently reviewable and revertible.

## Known limitations and follow-ups

- Notifications queued while the creator is busy are process-local. A host restart before the pending message drains can lose that queued delivery; a durable outbox is intentionally out of scope.
- The creator can inspect a child that needs input but cannot complete its pending input request from the creator conversation. #331541 tracks a typed response flow.

## Validation

- Agent Host unit suites: 460 passing, 17 pending.
- Copilot Agent Host provider E2E: 157 passing, 15 pending, including real `create_session` orchestration metadata publication.
- Copilot prompt snapshots: 21 passing across 19 model baselines.

## Type of issue

Code 1.133.0 (`a5b500951314efd502d07465bd138dfbd714a960`); current `main` is also affected.

macOS 26.5.2 arm64, 128 GiB system memory.

## Steps to reproduce

3. Inspect the `Mem MB` column.

## Actual

The process table reports impossible values such as:

```text
CPU %  Mem MB          PID  Process
0      360287970190  48139  code
1     1441151880759  48192  window [1]
```

The same processes report approximately 268 MiB and 1,085 MiB through `ps`.

## Cause

On non-Windows platforms, `listProcesses` already converts the `ps` memory percentage to bytes in `src/vs/base/node/ps.ts`. `DiagnosticsService.formatProcessItem` then treats that byte value as a percentage and multiplies by total system memory a second time. The Process Explorer correctly treats `ProcessItem.mem` as bytes.

## Expected

`code --status` should divide `ProcessItem.mem` by MiB directly on every platform, matching Process Explorer and the byte contract produced by `listProcesses`.

## Feature request

When a delegated agent session needs input, notify its creator and allow the creator to answer the pending request directly from the creator conversation.

Related orchestration work: #331521, foundation PR #331518, and notification PR #331544.

## Current behavior

The creator can be notified that a child needs input and can inspect the child's context. However, it cannot complete the pending input request from the creator session. Sending a normal message starts a separate turn and is not equivalent to answering the active request, so the user must open the child session to respond.

## Proposed behavior

Add a typed orchestration tool for responding to a child's active input request. It should:

- Target a specific child session and active request ID.
- Expose enough structured request context for the creator to form a valid response.
- Validate answers for the supported question type.
- Preserve explicit user confirmation for approvals or sensitive actions.
- Reject stale, completed, or mismatched requests.
- Respect the child's `coordinateWithCreator` policy.
- Work consistently across agent providers.

This would let a creator coordinate delegated work without leaving the parent conversation while avoiding the ambiguity and turn-state risks of treating a normal session message as an input response.

title: Copilot external ingest falls back to memory when workspace storage directory is absent
body:
Type: Bug

VS Code Stable 1.133.0 with bundled GitHub Copilot Chat 0.61.0 logs:

```text
Failed to create database. Falling back to in-memory db: Error: unable to open database file
```

The same construction remains on current main in Copilot Chat 0.63.0.

Cause:

`ExternalIngestIndex` joins `codebase-external.sqlite` onto `ExtensionContext.storageUri` and immediately passes the resulting path to `node:sqlite` `DatabaseSync`. The storage URI can be present while the extension-specific directory itself does not yet exist. SQLite can create the file but not its missing parent directory, so construction fails and the extension silently uses an in-memory index for that workspace.

This is distinct from permissions, corruption, and lock contention: the workspace-storage parent is writable, the extension-specific child is absent, and creating only that child makes the same bundled extension create and reopen the disk database successfully. Two cold starts then emitted no fallback, and both clean-close `PRAGMA integrity_check` runs returned `ok`.

Expected:

Before opening a file-backed external-ingest database, Copilot Chat should recursively create its declared file-scheme workspace-storage directory. A unit test should cover an absent nested storage directory and assert that `codebase-external.sqlite` is created there.

Related: #331190 includes the same database warning alongside a separate Windows extension-host crash, but this issue is limited to the deterministic missing-directory fallback.

title: "The PR workflow skill is unavailable in this checkout"
body: ## Type Bug ## Summary An active Agent Host session can retain skill paths under one synchronized-customization nonce while a later `session/activeClientSet` publication materializes a new nonce for the same plugin identity. `AgentPluginManager` immediately deletes the older nonce directory, after which invoking an advertised skill fails with `ENOENT`. This is the underlying cache-lifetime problem also visible in #328464, but it is not specific to `/act-on-feedback`. The latest reproduction involved the built-in synchronized `create-pr` skill. ## Reproduction observed 1. An Agent Host session was using a synchronized plugin revision under nonce A. 2. The user requested that the agent create a pull request. 3. During that turn, the client published an updated customization set for the session's workspace-scoped bundle with nonce B. 4. The host materialized nonce B and immediately logged `Evicting stale nonce for plugin` for nonce A. 5. Less than one second later, the model invoked `skill("create-pr")` using the path that had been advertised from nonce A. 6. The skill tool failed with an error shaped like: ```text Failed to read skill file: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/agentPlugins///skills/create-pr/SKILL.md' ``` The plugin subsequently moved through additional nonces and eventually recreated nonce A, explaining why the missing file can exist again when the cache is inspected after the incident. ## Actual behavior `AgentPluginManager._syncPlugin` materializes the new revision and then calls `_cleanupStaleNoncesFor`, which deletes every revision except the most recently used one. Active sessions retain concrete paths into those nonce directories, but the cache has no explicit ownership or lease tying those paths to session lifetime. The implementation relies on deletion failing when an old revision is still in use. That does not work as a lifetime mechanism on macOS/Unix: retaining or reading a pathname does not keep its directory from being deleted. The current unit test explicitly expects the previous nonce directory to be deleted immediately after syncing a new nonce, so it does not cover an active session retaining the returned path. ## Expected behavior - A customization path advertised to an active session remains readable for as long as that session can invoke it. - Installing a new nonce for the same plugin identity does not invalidate paths retained by other active sessions or turns. - Cache cleanup uses explicit ownership/lifetime information rather than filesystem deletion failure as a proxy for whether a revision is in use. - If an advertised synchronized skill becomes unavailable anyway, the host refreshes or re-resolves it rather than returning an unrecoverable `ENOENT`. ## Related changes - #320854 introduced per-nonce plugin directories and immediate stale-nonce eviction. The stated intent was to allow long-running sessions to keep referencing older revisions, but the lock-based retention mechanism does not provide that guarantee. - #330378 introduced workspace-scoped synchronized bundle identities and was intended to stop cross-workspace nonce ping-pong. In this reproduction, its scoped active-client reconciler published the nonce replacement that exposed the unsafe eviction. The same scoped bundle still changed nonces repeatedly, so the expected stable-nonce invariant did not hold. - #330413 and #330803 made adjacent cache fixes for missing entries and initialization serialization, but do not change the active-revision lifetime problem. - #328464 reports the same missing-backing-file symptom for `/act-on-feedback`. ## Suggested fix Track explicit leases/reference counts for materialized `(plugin URI, nonce)` revisions: 1. Acquire a lease when a synced revision is handed to a session/provider. 2. Release it when that session is disposed or switches revisions. 3. Evict only unreferenced revisions. 4. Add a regression test that retains nonce A's returned directory, syncs nonce B, verifies nonce A remains readable, then releases A and verifies it becomes eligible for cleanup. As a short-term mitigation, avoid immediate stale-nonce deletion until cleanup can run at a lifecycle boundary that knows no active session retains the revision. (Written by Copilot)

title: Read project customizations on the host's own filesystem
body:
Fixes #331526.

In a remote window the agent host reads project-scope customizations off a URI it cannot resolve, so it finds none. The symptom users hit is that a new chat offers no workspace slash commands until a turn has run.

The window hands the session its working directory in the client's namespace. A diagnostic build of the host logged, for a fresh chat in a dev container:

```
workingDirectory = vscode-remote://dev-container+<hex>/workspace/printstream
userHome         = file:///home/node
```

The host runs inside that container and its file service only answers for `file:`, and `getSessionCustomizations` passes the working directory straight to four disk scans (agents/skills/commands, rules, MCP servers, hooks). Each returns empty rather than raising, so the customizations are absent with nothing in the log.

### Fix

A conversion beside the other agent-host URI helpers, applied only to reads the host performs itself:

```ts
export function toHostLocalUri(resource: URI): URI {
	if (resource.scheme !== Schemas.vscodeRemote) {
		return resource;
	}
	return URI.file(resource.fsPath);
}
```

The path is the part both namespaces agree on, which materialize already relies on by handing the SDK `workingDirectory.fsPath` as its cwd. This applies the same reading to the host's own disk access.

Deliberately narrow:

- **Only `vscode-remote:`.** Stripping the authority off any other scheme would name a local file that is not there rather than the resource meant. A local window compares `file:` to `file:` and is untouched.
- **Only host-side reads.** `workingDirectory` and `workingDirectories` are unchanged for everything else; anything sent back to the client, or compared against client-supplied URIs, keeps the namespace the client uses.

### Verification

- Unit tests for the conversion: the remote rewrite, a `file:` no-op, a non-remote scheme left alone, and that the client authority never leaks into a host read.
- Verified live in a dev-container window. Before: 17 suggestions in a fresh chat, none of them the project's six commands. After: 23, with all six present and no turn run.
- An equivalent command placed in `~/.claude/commands/` was offered before the first turn both before and after the fix, which isolates the failure to project scope rather than to the suggestion pipeline.
- The `file:` URI shape this produces is one the client already resolves: a user-scope command, which has always been surfaced as a host-local `file:` URI, resolves and runs end to end. So project entries now arrive in a shape with a working precedent rather than a new one.

### What is not covered

The conversion is unit-tested and the wiring is verified live, but there is no unit test asserting that `getSessionCustomizations` passes the converted form, because that needs a fully constructed session and the existing tests stub the method rather than exercise it. I would rather say so than imply coverage that is not there.

The Codex customization scan takes working directories the same way and joins onto them, so it looks like the same shape. I have not reproduced it there and have left it out of this change.

```
userHome         = file:///home/node
```

The host runs inside the container, and its file service only answers for `file:`. `getSessionCustomizations` passes that working directory straight to four disk scans:

```ts
discoverClaudeMultiRootCustomizations(this.workingDirectories, userHome, …),  // agents, skills, commands
scanClaudeRules(this.workingDirectory, userHome, …),
scanClaudeMcpServers(this.workingDirectory, userHome, …),
scanClaudeHooks(this.workingDirectory, userHome, …),
```

so each reads a URI it cannot resolve. It fails quietly: the scan returns empty rather than raising, so the customizations are simply absent with nothing in the log.

Two details explain why this looks narrower than it is:

- **User scope still works**, because `userHome` is already a host-local `file:` URI. That is what makes the symptom present as "`.claude/commands` is ignored" rather than "project scope is ignored".
- **Slash commands appear to recover after the first turn**, but only because the SDK then supplies its own command list. The disk scan never starts working, so project rules, MCP servers and hooks stay invisible even after materialize.

### Reproduction

In a dev-container window, with commands in `<workspace>/.claude/commands/`:

1. Open a new chat and type `/`. The project's commands are absent.
2. Send any message.
3. Type `/` again. They are now listed.

Measured on the suggest widget: 17 entries before the first turn, none of them the project's six commands; 23 after, with all six present. Placing an equivalent command in `~/.claude/commands/` instead makes it appear immediately, before any turn, which isolates the failure to project scope.

### Scope

The Codex customization scan takes working directories the same way and joins onto them (`URI.joinPath(workingDirectory, '.github', 'agents')`), so it looks like the same shape. I have not reproduced it there, so I am noting it rather than claiming it.

title: Improve workspace resolution in agent session tools
body:
Fixes #330948

## Expected user benefits

- Ask an agent to start work in a known project by display name instead of supplying an exact filesystem path.
- Start delegated work from the configured project root rather than accidentally reusing a transient worktree.
- Discover remote project URIs and every folder in a multi-root session through the existing `list_sessions` tool.
- Pass a returned project or working-directory URI directly to `create_session`.
- Receive explicit candidate URIs when a project name is ambiguous instead of silently choosing the wrong workspace.
- Preserve the existing compact fields for model and client compatibility.

## Changes

- Keep workspace discovery within the existing `list_sessions` and `create_session` tools rather than adding another model-visible tool.
- Add `projectUri` to serialized sessions while preserving the human-readable `project` field.
- Add `workingDirectories` for multi-root sessions while preserving the primary `workingDirectory` field.
- Let the `list_sessions.workspace` filter match a project display name, project URI, or any working directory.
- Let `create_session.workspace` resolve a unique project display name to its configured project root.
- Reject ambiguous project names with the candidate project URIs.
- Compare parsed workspace URIs with URI comparison semantics instead of string-key deduplication.
- Cover remote URIs, multi-root metadata, configured-root preference, ambiguous names, and remote cross-provider creation.

## Design rationale

Workspace metadata already comes from known session metadata, so a separate `list_workspaces` tool would be another projection of the same authority and would add its description and schema to every model prompt. Extending the existing tools closes the actual information gap with no extra always-advertised tool:

1. `list_sessions({ includeArchived: true, workspace: "Visual Studio Code" })` can locate matching known sessions and returns the configured `projectUri` plus working directories.
2. `create_session({ workspace: "Visual Studio Code", ... })` resolves the name directly when unique.
3. The agent can pass an explicit returned URI when several projects share a name.

Provider selection remains model-driven, as it is today. A test verifies that a remote project URI discovered from one session can be used to create a session with a model from another provider.

## Scope

Only projects already visible through known Agent Host sessions are resolved by name. A global recent-workspace catalog, fuzzy ranking, and new-folder permission flows remain out of scope.

## Follow-up

- #331553 tracks starting an agent session without a folder and binding the existing conversation to a workspace later, after the request or context identifies the appropriate project.

## Validation

- TypeScript compilation passes.
- Session tool and display suites: 53 passing.
- Copilot prompt snapshots: 21 passing across 19 model baselines.
- Copilot Agent Host provider E2E: 157 passing, 15 pending.

body:
Cherry-pick of #331506 from `release/1.134`.

Fixes #331452

## Impact
After an update, existing local Agent Host sessions can permanently disappear from the Agents Window. Conversation history remains on disk, but lost registry/cache entries make the sessions inaccessible. This is user-visible session data loss.

## Root cause
A transient SDK startup failure can return an unavailable session catalog. Migration treated that as success, allowing `listSessions()` to return an incomplete registry that the client reconciled as deleted sessions.

## Fix
Treat an unavailable catalog as a failed migration, retry before listing, and reject if it remains unavailable. The client then preserves its cache and uses its existing backoff retry instead of accepting a partial catalog.

title: Agent sessions: coordinate independently scoped child sessions

labels.name: feature-request

body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

Some tasks genuinely require independent units of work across repositories, workspaces, branches/worktrees, providers, or lifecycles. Today, users and agents must manually create those sessions, track progress, move context between them, and decide when their results are ready to integrate.

## Product model

A session is the user-visible unit of work: one workspace/worktree, lifecycle, and aggregate diff. Parallel subtasks that share that unit should use chats within the session.

Cross-session delegation is the complementary path for work that must be independently scoped and resumable.

## Example workflow

A user asks an agent to implement a feature spanning separate client and server repositories. The creator session should be able to:

1. Resolve each workspace and create one child session per independently scoped workstream.
2. Give each child a focused task, label, and optional model/provider.
3. Continue coordinating while the children run independently.
4. Be notified when a child finishes, needs input, or fails.
5. Inspect each result and summarize or integrate it for the user.

## Proposed experience

- Prefer same-session chats when parallel work should share one workspace and aggregate diff.
- Allow an agent to create and message child sessions for independent repositories, workspaces, branches/worktrees, providers, or lifecycles.
- Keep the creator session and its aggregate result primary.
- Surface child relationships, labels, status, workspace/worktree, and linked PR when useful, without making implementation-detail children dominate the session list.
- Let users open a child to inspect or redirect independently scoped work.
- Return completion or failure signals without interrupting an active creator turn.
- Let the creator collect bounded child context and synthesize the final result.

## Acceptance criteria

- Tool guidance distinguishes same-session chat delegation from independently scoped child sessions.
- A creator can run at least two independently scoped child sessions concurrently.
- Each child has an explicit task, workspace, status, and discoverable relationship to its creator.
- The creator receives reliable completion, input-needed, and error signals.
- The creator can inspect child results without manual copy/paste.
- Users can tell where child changes live and how to open or integrate them.
- Delegation honors existing confirmation, trust, permission, and concurrency controls.

## Related issues

- #282818 — one-click delegation to multiple agents
- #286547 — multiple background agents from Copilot Chat
- #296469 — dynamic cross-model delegation
- #317195 — notifications when sessions need attention or finish
- #330948 — workspace resolution for agent session tools
- #331541 — answer child input from the creator session
- #331554 — surface cross-session delegation without obscuring aggregate work

Implementation:

- #331518 — cross-session delegation relationships and notifications
- #331525 — workspace resolution through existing session tools

title: Add cross-session delegation and notifications
body:
Part of microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#8366.
Part of #331521.

## Scope

A session remains the user-visible unit of work: one workspace/worktree, lifecycle, and aggregate diff. `create_chat` is the preferred primitive for parallel subtasks that should stay within that unit.

This PR adds coordination for the complementary cross-session case, where delegated work needs an independent workspace, worktree or branch, provider, or lifecycle.

## Expected user benefits

- Delegate independently scoped work across repositories, workspaces, or branches.
- Discover delegated sessions through durable creator/parent relationships and labels.
- Inspect child context, steer work, and receive completion or input-needed notifications without polling.
- Keep fire-and-forget work isolated by disabling direct child-to-creator coordination.

## Changes

- Guide models to prefer `create_chat` for shared-workspace subtasks and reserve `create_session` for independently scoped work.
- Persist creator identity separately from hierarchy placement, with an optional label and coordination policy.
- Extend `create_session` with `coordinateWithCreator`, `notifyOnIdle`, and `label`.
- Extend `list_sessions` with parent and label filters and expose permitted orchestration metadata.
- Enforce disabled creator coordination across relationship discovery and prompt-producing tools.
- Restore persisted orchestration metadata and notification state.
- Deliver opt-in input-needed, idle, and error notifications through a dedicated coordination service, queueing behind active creator work.

## Alignment with GitHub Copilot app

The relationship and notification primitives align with the GitHub Copilot app, while VS Code additionally distinguishes chats within a session. The App-style session workflow remains available for genuinely independent work; same-session orchestration should use chats so users retain one aggregate diff.

## Follow-ups

- #331554 tracks delegated-work UX; the parent session and its aggregate result should remain primary.
- #331541 tracks answering a child's pending input request directly from the creator.

title: Automations should not rename themselves

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: automations
labels.description: Issue for the sessions window automation feature

body:
Now that the automations view is using the session flat list, the name of the run is no longer controlled by the view. Agents typically name their session as they start a turn, so either we need some alternate way to correlate an automation with its run, or we should prevent agents from renaming a session when it detects its an automation.

When automations moves to the agent host there should be a flag that the agent host can check for when considering a rename. Until then, we may need some other fix around this.

## AI investigation

The current behavior spans two naming paths:

- [`AutomationRunner`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/sessions/contrib/automations/browser/automationRunner.ts) starts the background request with `title: automation.name`, then persists the returned session resource on the automation run.
- [`AutomationHistorySection`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/views/automationsView.ts) resolves each run to an `ISession` and passes those sessions to `SessionsFlatList`.
- [`SessionsFlatList` / `SessionItemRenderer`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/views/sessionsList.ts) renders the session's observable title. As a result, a later agent-driven chat rename becomes the visible run name instead of the automation name.

There is already an `ISession.isAutomation` observable, but for local Agent Host sessions it is currently populated by [`LocalAgentHostSessionsProvider`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/browser/localAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts) by matching session resources against persisted automation runs. That happens in the browser after the run has been linked to its created session, so it is not available early enough to suppress first-turn renaming inside Agent Host.

The Agent Host decision points are [`AgentHostSessionTitleController.seedTitleFromFirstMessage`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostSessionTitleController.ts) and `prepareInstructionForAgent`. The latter supplies the `rename_chat` reminder when active-agent title generation is enabled. Once automations are owned by Agent Host, an automation flag on `SessionState` could be checked at those points before seeding a title or asking the agent to rename the chat.

Until that flag exists in Agent Host, possible short-term options are:

1. Keep the history row correlated with its automation by having the Automations view provide the automation name when rendering the linked session.
2. Propagate an automation marker during programmatic session creation through [`ISessionsManagementService`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/sessions/services/sessions/browser/sessionsManagementService.ts) into Agent Host session state, then check it in the title controller.

title: Add standalone Copilot source build pipeline
body:
## Summary

- add a standalone pipeline that builds the Copilot SDK and all runtime targets from source
- publish the source-built npm packages to the internal VS Code feed
- queue the existing product build with `VSCODE_SDK_CANARY_VERSION` and `VSCODE_CLI_CANARY_VERSION` overrides
- leave the existing product pipeline unchanged
- run artifact-based sanity tests when the queued product build is unpublished
- incorporate the review feedback from #330768

## Validation

- `node --experimental-strip-types --test build/lib/test/copilotSourcePipeline.test.ts build/lib/test/copilot.test.ts` (24 tests passed)
- pre-commit hygiene
- [Current Copilot source validation 466127](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=466127) is running against validation commit `138e7825393` based on PR head `759646de601`; product publish and release are disabled
- Prior [Copilot source pipeline 465834](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=465834) succeeded for all eight runtime targets and published `0.0.0-vscode.1.134.0.465834`
- Prior [product build 465837](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=465837) succeeded across all stages with the SDK/runtime overrides

## Failure investigation

[Initial run 464620](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=464620) exposed direct Corepack, Cargo, and PyPI access blocked by 1ES network isolation. The pipeline now provisions the runtime-pinned pnpm through authenticated npm, uses the internal Cargo and Python feeds, installs target-capable rustup alongside RustInstaller, and downloads each runtime artifact by explicit name.

Supersedes #330768.

## Upstream build overlap and future simplification

No upstream implementation is copied verbatim. Of the approximately 1,755 production lines added here:

- roughly 300 lines reimplement release/package behavior such as version stamping, package metadata assembly, source-map policy, and publication checks
- roughly 350–450 lines mirror upstream build orchestration and entrypoint contracts while delegating the actual builds
- roughly 1,000–1,100 lines are VS Code/Azure-specific authentication, internal-feed, artifact, validation, and product-build integration

For the SDK, this pipeline delegates compilation to the SDK repository’s build command but currently mirrors its install, version, package, and publish sequence. For the private runtime repository, this pipeline delegates native compilation, JavaScript bundling, and package staging to repository-owned entrypoints; it does not reproduce those implementations. VS Code owns secure checkout, target fan-out, toolchain/feed setup, artifact validation, internal package publication, and the product-build handoff.

A useful follow-up would be stable upstream entrypoints that emit publish-ready artifacts:

- an SDK entrypoint accepting the desired package version and runtime dependency version and returning an npm tarball
- a runtime entrypoint accepting target and version inputs and returning a final platform package, ideally alongside a supported-target manifest

With those contracts, we could substantially simplify or remove `buildCopilotOverride.ts`, much of `copilotRuntimeSource.ts`, `install-runtime-build-toolchain.ts`, the runtime package assembly in `copilotSourcePublish.ts`, and most of `source-publish-runtime-job.yml`. Package-only entrypoints would remove an estimated 300–450 lines; entrypoints that also own toolchain/bootstrap behavior could remove approximately 600–800 lines.

The runtime references above intentionally describe contracts and responsibilities only; they do not quote or link to private source.

## Authoritative build overrides

The mechanism supports a generic `package.json` `buildOverrides` map from package name to immutable source commit. The Copilot source pipeline reads those values directly; it no longer accepts SDK/runtime source-ref parameters. This PR intentionally leaves the map absent after validation, so normal product builds remain unchanged; a branch adds the map only when it intentionally needs source-built dependencies. Internal package versions are deterministic from the VS Code version and full VS Code commit, and the child product build is pinned to that exact branch and commit.

Every published source package carries provenance metadata for the VS Code commit, source commit, dependency version, and diagnostic source-build ID. Product builds automatically detect committed Copilot overrides, reconstruct the expected internal version, validate provenance, and apply it. If matching packages were not published, the build fails with a link to the Copilot source pipeline. This failure is intentional while an override is committed: it must never be silently ignored. The validated overrides were removed from this PR after the successful source/product build runs. Manual SDK canary parameters remain supported only when no Copilot `buildOverrides` are present.

title: agentHost: Reject unavailable session catalogs
body:
Fixes #331452

(cherry picked from commit [dcc387ba7e912c3d25e43cc5b064b9fecc3427c2](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/331506))

## Impact
After an update, existing local Agent Host sessions can permanently disappear from the Agents Window. Conversation history remains on disk, but lost registry/cache entries make the sessions inaccessible. This is user-visible session data loss.

## Root cause
A transient SDK startup failure can return an unavailable session catalog. Migration treated that as success, allowing `listSessions()` to return an incomplete registry that the client reconciled as deleted sessions.

## Fix
Treat an unavailable catalog as a failed migration, retry before listing, and reject if it remains unavailable. The client then preserves its cache and uses its existing backoff retry instead of accepting a partial catalog.

## Validation
- `npm run compile`
- `npm run hygiene`
- 492 affected tests passed

title: Multi-root: a folder's customization is unreachable when another folder defines the same name

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

body:
Testing #331067

- VS Code Version: 1.134.0-insider (`fc62850c022bbba2c93b0202dd24f42d1e0b3882`, 2026-08-16)
- OS Version: macOS (darwin arm64)
- Harness: Claude

Refs #321651

In a multi-root workspace, when two folders each contribute a customization with the **same name**, the primary folder's copy wins and the other folder's copy becomes **unreachable by any name**, with no diagnostic that it was shadowed.

Two repos in one workspace both having a `deploy` skill (or a `reviewer` agent, or a `ship` command) seems like the common case rather than a corner case, and today the second repo's version is silently unusable.

### Steps to Reproduce

Create a throwaway workspace where two folders define a skill with the same name, plus a uniquely-named control skill:

```bash
ROOT=~/mr-repro; rm -rf "$ROOT"; mkdir -p "$ROOT"

# folder-a and folder-b both define a skill named "deploy", with distinct markers
for f in folder-a folder-b; do
  mkdir -p "$ROOT/$f/.claude/skills/deploy"
  cat > "$ROOT/$f/.claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md" <<EOF
---
name: deploy
description: Deploy probe. Use when asked to run the deploy skill.
---

Reply with exactly this marker and nothing else:

DEPLOY-FROM-${f##*-}
EOF
done

# control: a UNIQUELY named skill in folder-b
mkdir -p "$ROOT/folder-b/.claude/skills/only-in-b"
cat > "$ROOT/folder-b/.claude/skills/only-in-b/SKILL.md" <<'EOF'
---
name: only-in-b
description: Uniquely named control skill. Use when asked to run the only-in-b skill.
---

Reply with exactly this marker and nothing else:

ONLY-IN-B-OK
EOF

cat > "$ROOT/repro.code-workspace" <<'EOF'
{
	"folders": [ { "path": "folder-a" }, { "path": "folder-b" } ],
	"settings": {}
}
EOF
```

With these in **User** settings (they are `included: false`, so they must be typed by hand):

```jsonc
{
  "chat.agentHost.claudeAgent.enabled": true,
  "chat.agentHost.claudeAgent.multiRootEnabled": true
}
```

1. **File → Open Workspace from File…** → `~/mr-repro/repro.code-workspace`
2. New chat, session target **Claude**, leave the Folder chip on **`folder-a`** (the default primary).
3. Send: `Run the deploy skill, then the only-in-b skill. Report each exact marker on its own line.`
4. Send: `Use the Skill tool with each of these exact skill values, one at a time, and report verbatim what the tool returns: "folder-b:deploy", "folder-b/deploy", "deploy (folder-b)".`

### Expected

Either a scoped name for the shadowed copy — agent-plugin skills already surface this way, e.g. `my-plugin:my-skill` — or at minimum some indication that a discovered customization was shadowed.

### Actual

| Skill value | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `deploy` | `DEPLOY-FROM-a` — the primary's copy wins |
| `only-in-b` | `ONLY-IN-B-OK` — **control passes** |
| `folder-b:deploy` | `Unknown skill: folder-b:deploy` |
| `folder-b/deploy` | `Unknown skill: folder-b/deploy` |
| `deploy (folder-b)` | `Unknown skill: deploy (folder-b)` |

`DEPLOY-FROM-b` is unreachable. Those `Unknown skill` strings are the raw tool results read from the agent host trace log, not the model's summary.

**The control is the important part:** `only-in-b` resolves fine, so `folder-b`'s customizations *are* being discovered and invoked. This is specifically collision handling, not a discovery failure. The registry exposes `deploy` exactly once, unprefixed.

Same behavior for a colliding **custom agent** (two folders each defining an agent with the same name).

### Notes

Shadowing itself looks deliberate — `claudeAgentSkillScan.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * Merges parsed components into a name→component map. First-seen wins, so
 * scanning project before user (and skills before commands) makes the
 * earlier entry shadow same-named later ones deterministically.
 */
function collectByName<T extends INamedPluginResource>(into: Map<string, T>, items: readonly T[]): void {
	for (const item of items) {
		if (!into.has(item.name)) { into.set(item.name, item); }
	}
}
```

That reads as written for project-vs-user precedence. The multi-root consequence looks like a side effect rather than an intent — so filing this as a **design gap** rather than a straight bug.

Worth noting `mapDiscoveredCustomizations` already buckets customizations per working directory, so the folder attribution needed to disambiguate is available at that point; the name is collapsed anyway, and the SDK's `Unknown skill` is the downstream symptom.

`collectByName` is unchanged on `main` as of 2026-08-18 (last touched by #328207), so this should still reproduce there — though I verified on `fc62850c022`, not on a `main` build.

**Not verified for Copilot or Codex**, whose customization scans are separate. That comparison would show how broad any fix needs to be; I can run it as part of the Codex pass for #331067.
