title: Chat session history randomly disappears from the Chat panel when the workspace folder is on a NAS (UNC path)
body:
**Type of issue:** Bug

**VS Code version:** 1.133.0 (x64) — observed across recent 1.12x–1.13x versions

**OS version:** Windows 11 Home 10.0.26200

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Open a workspace folder located on a NAS via a UNC path, e.g. 
2. Use the Chat panel normally over several days so sessions accumulate (stored in `%APPDATA%\Code\User\globalStorage\github.copilot-chat\session-store.db` and per-workspace `workspaceStorage\<hash>\state.vscdb`).
3. At random intervals (observed: every few days), reopen the same folder — the Chat history panel is empty or shows only a subset of the sessions.

**Actual behavior:** Sessions disappear from the Chat history UI at random intervals when the workspace is on a NAS. The data is **not deleted**: the SQLite stores on disk still contain all sessions, and they can be fully recovered by merging the `chat.ChatSessionStore.index` from another workspaceStorage folder into the current one. Investigation showed the same physical NAS folder had been assigned different `workspaceStorage` hashes over time (`d04b0ded6d4405b53bbedxxxxxxx` vs `d92c9503309f26060f5107xxxxxxxxx`), i.e. the workspace identity changed even though it is the same folder. Suspected root cause: how/when the UNC path is resolved (UNC vs mapped drive, hostname vs IP, NAS briefly unreachable at startup) changes the workspace identity, and each identity gets its own per-workspace chat store — so history appears to "vanish" from the UI while still existing on disk under the other hash.

**Expected behavior:** The same physical folder on a NAS should always resolve to the same workspace identity and the same chat session store, regardless of mount state or path spelling.

**Additional context:** Reproduced with the built-in Copilot/chat feature of VS Code 1.133 (bundled, no separate extension). Chat session sync (`chat.sessionSync.enabled`) is not involved — it is experimental and no cloud sync occurs in this scenario.

Instead, it introduces a stable marker class for decoration colors, updates the code to apply this marker, and refactors CSS selectors to use direct class matches. These changes prevent expensive style recalculations and improve overall responsiveness, especially in large workbench instances.

| Scenario | Before | After | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Full style recalc — Modern UI **off** | 1.35 ms | 0.57 ms | **−58%** |
| Full style recalc — Modern UI **on** | 1.42 ms | 0.57 ms | **−60%** |
| Full style recalc — stacked on base `.codicon[class*=…]` rules | 2.80 ms | 2.13 ms | **−24%** |
| Tree row focus change (arrow-key nav) | 0.06 ms | 0.06 ms | unchanged |
| Tab switch | 0.02 ms | 0.02 ms | unchanged |

**CSS performance and selector improvements:**

* Updated CSS best practices documentation to strongly discourage substring matching on the `class` attribute (e.g., `[class*="…"]`), explaining the significant performance impact and recommending the use of a stable marker class instead (`DECORATION_LABEL_COLOR_CLASS`).
* Refactored all relevant CSS selectors in `tabs.css` and test fixture CSS to use direct class selectors (`.monaco-decoration-itemColor`) instead of substring matches, ensuring efficient style invalidation. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b64014d5040ac599efbe8316b68bcf50db31073aa12d3d14aa79bb24773f841aR905-R925) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b64014d5040ac599efbe8316b68bcf50db31073aa12d3d14aa79bb24773f841aL928-R940) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b64014d5040ac599efbe8316b68bcf50db31073aa12d3d14aa79bb24773f841aL943-R962) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-1a0779d8943b6feb1ad01bc47d9578fd204e97e1ae835607d5d2d3efc23931a9L10-R10)

**Stable marker class introduction and usage:**

* Introduced the constant `DECORATION_LABEL_COLOR_CLASS` in `decorations.ts` as a stable marker for decoration color classes, with detailed documentation on its purpose and usage.
* Updated the resource label widget logic in `labels.ts` to always add both the stable marker class and the generated decoration color class to decorated labels, ensuring consistent marker application. title: Rename chat tool in editor window does not seem to have effect

body:
## Reproduction steps

1. In the regular editor window, create a new **Agent Host Copilot** chat editor.
2. Send a prompt and wait for the session to receive a title. Note the current editor-tab and session-list title.
3. While remaining in that chat, ask:

   > Use `create_chat` to create another chat in this current session. Give it the title `Sibling Chat` and the prompt `Reply exactly READY`.

4. Wait for `create_chat` to complete, but do **not** navigate away from the original chat.
5. In the original chat, ask:

   > Call `rename_chat` for this current chat with the title `Multi Chat Rename Test`. Do not call any other tool.

6. Confirm the `rename_chat` invocation targets the current chat. Its input should normally be:

   ```json
   {
     "title": "Multi Chat Rename Test"
   }
   ```

## Actual behavior

The tool reports `Renamed chat to "Multi Chat Rename Test".`, but the original editor tab and session-list entry retain their old titles. Closing and reopening the chat may also restore the old title.

## Expected behavior

The original editor tab and session-list entry update to **Multi Chat Rename Test**, and the title remains correct after closing and reopening the chat.

title: sessions: fix: clear stale Agent Host input-needed status
body:
## Summary

Fix false-positive **Input needed** status in the Agents window when a visible Agent Host session keeps working after a confirmation has been resolved.

## Root cause

The Agent Host protocol already cleared the input request and changed the aggregate session state back to `InProgress`. However, the Agents-window provider used its live `SessionState` subscription only to synchronize configuration, metadata, changesets, and the per-chat catalog.

The top-level `ISession` status and activity were updated only by root summary notifications or a later `listSessions()` refresh. This allowed the session row to retain an older `NeedsInput` value while a subagent or peer chat continued running.

## Fix

- Reconcile the top-level session status and activity from each subscribed `SessionState` snapshot.
- Keep read and archive flags synchronized through the same path.
- Share protocol-status translation between live snapshots and root summary notifications.
- Emit the existing provider change event only when the adapted values change.
- Document the live-snapshot ownership contract for visible Agent Host sessions.

This does not suppress legitimate confirmations, change protocol status precedence, special-case subagents, or add polling.

## Test plan

- Added a regression where:
  - the list snapshot starts at `InputNeeded`;
  - confirmation has been resolved;
  - the subscribed session state is `InProgress`;
  - a tool-origin subagent chat remains active.
- Verified that the top-level session immediately exposes `InProgress`, current activity text, and the correct read state without waiting for turn completion or a session-list refresh.
- Full `LocalAgentHostSessionsProvider` suite: **191 passing, 11 pending**
- ESLint on both changed TypeScript files
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run transpile-client`
- `git diff --check`
